description: Retrieval test set: a small, deliberately overlapping research library (sleep/memory, coral reefs, RAG notes, lab notebook, meeting minutes). Each passage is ingested as its own document so a hit is judged at passage level. Every query has exactly one gold passage, identified by a substring that appears nowhere else. Query types: keyword = exact identifiers, numbers or names; paraphrase = little or no word overlap with the answer; precision = several passages share the keywords, only one answers; identifier = the query is just a code or name with no context words (this group was added after the first run, which showed the keyword group always had semantic words around the identifier).

tmr_spindles_study: We tested whether replaying sounds linked to learned word pairs during slow-wave sleep strengthens declarative memory. Sixty-two undergraduates learned 120 word pairs, each paired with a unique sound, before an overnight session in the sleep lab.
During slow-wave sleep, half of the sounds were replayed at low volume. Participants recalled cued pairs better than uncued pairs the next morning, with an average advantage of 11 percent.
The benefit depended on sleep spindles. Cues followed within two seconds by a spindle burst were remembered far more often than cues that produced no spindle.
Replaying the same sounds during REM sleep in a control group produced no measurable advantage for cued items.
Items that were weakly learned before sleep gained the most from reactivation, whereas strongly encoded pairs showed a ceiling effect.
aging_sleep_review: Older adults spend markedly less time in slow-wave sleep than young adults, and the decline begins in middle age.
Spindle density falls by roughly a third between the third and seventh decades of life, which may explain part of the age-related loss in overnight memory retention.
Atrophy of the medial prefrontal cortex correlates with reduced slow-wave activity, linking structural brain changes to sleep quality in elderly participants.
Only two small studies have tried cueing memories during sleep in people over sixty-five, and neither found a reliable benefit.
Acoustic stimulation timed to slow oscillation up-states can boost slow waves in older listeners, but effects on memory remain inconsistent across labs.
sleep_deprivation_wm: Forty adults stayed awake for 36 hours under supervision before completing an n-back task.
Accuracy on the 3-back condition dropped by 14 percent after deprivation, while the 1-back condition was largely unaffected.
Caffeine at 200 mg restored reaction times but did not restore accuracy on the hardest working memory load.
Recovery sleep of eight hours returned performance to baseline in most participants, although two individuals still showed deficits.
Self-rated sleepiness was a poor predictor of who would make the most errors.
coral_acclimation: Marine heatwaves in 2016 and 2017 caused mass bleaching along the Great Barrier Reef.
Reefs exposed to moderate heat stress in 2016 lost 31 percent fewer corals when the 2017 heatwave arrived.
The protective effect vanished once heat stress exceeded eight degree heating weeks.
Branching Acropora colonies bleached first and died fastest, while massive Porites colonies mostly recovered.
Projections suggest severe bleaching will become an annual event on most reefs by 2050.
coral_symbionts: Corals host single-celled algae of the family Symbiodiniaceae that supply most of their energy.
After bleaching, some colonies were recolonized by the heat-tolerant genus Durusdinium, which raised their thermal threshold by about one degree Celsius.
The tolerance came at a cost: colonies dominated by Durusdinium grew 38 percent more slowly than those hosting Cladocopium.
Shuffling was rare in colonies deeper than ten metres, where water stays cooler during heatwaves.
Microbiome sequencing found that bacterial communities shifted within days of bleaching, long before algal symbionts changed.
rag_notes: Retrieval-augmented generation lets a language model answer from documents it was not trained on by fetching relevant passages at query time.
Dense retrievers embed queries and passages into the same vector space, but they often miss exact identifiers such as product codes or gene names.
BM25 keyword search handles rare terms well but cannot match paraphrases that share no words with the query.
Combining both with reciprocal rank fusion is a common, robust baseline.
A cross-encoder reranker reads each query and passage together and usually improves the ordering of the top results, at the price of extra latency.
lab_notebook: Protocol P-17 replaced the old cueing script; volume is now fixed at 42 dB and cues stop if an arousal is detected.
Cohort B3 had to be excluded after the EEG amplifier logged corrupted files on nights four through six.
Participant S-208 reported hearing the cues, so their data were moved to the awareness-check analysis.
The Hypnodyne headband underestimated slow-wave sleep by about twenty minutes compared with lab polysomnography.
Ethics amendment EA-2024-031 was approved, allowing us to recruit adults up to age seventy-five.
meeting_notes: We agreed that the next study should test whether boosting spindles with closed-loop audio can rescue memory reactivation in older adults.
Funding from the Wellcome pilot scheme ends in June, so data collection must finish by April.
Reviewer two asked for a power analysis; the current sample of sixty-two gives about eighty percent power for a medium effect.
The reef team will share their temperature logger pipeline so we can reuse it for ambient bedroom monitoring.
Everyone should move raw files to the encrypted lab drive; personal laptops are no longer allowed for participant data.
